turns.request: Please furnish our new flat in Orion on the top floor. We are Arman (36) and Siranush (34) Petrosyan with two kids, Tigran (7) and Nare (4). Arman is a game developer at a studio in Yerevan and works from home four days a week: he needs a real office with a 160 cm desk, two monitors, a good chair, shelves for his board-game collection and a door he can close for calls. The small reading room next to the bedrooms is his office. Siranush is a pediatric dentist, out early, back at six; in the evenings she reads and does pilates at home, so she wants a clear spot for a yoga mat in the living room. Tigran and Nare share one bedroom for now: Tigran loves dinosaurs and Lego and needs a little desk for homework, Nare still naps and loves drawing. They need two beds (a bunk bed is fine if it is safe), lots of low toy storage they can reach themselves, a soft rug to play on and a reading nook. We take the other bedroom: a queen bed, a wardrobe and a dresser, nothing fancy. The big living room with the kitchen is where everything happens: a dining table for six (grandparents come every Friday), a large sofa that survives kids, a TV for movie nights, and a corner where the kids can play without toys taking over the whole room. The balcony: two chairs and a small table for morning coffee, plus plants. Style: bright Scandinavian with warm oak, soft pastels, rounded corners (no sharp glass tables with kids), washable fabrics. We dislike dark colours and anything fragile. Budget: 7,500,000 AMD for furniture.

proposal.title: Please furnish our new flat in Orion on the top floor

Both revised rooms were rendered and visually reviewed, and the whole-flat check passes. Furniture totals **5,652,500 AMD**, within your **7,500,000 AMD** budget; finishes and lighting are priced separately.

[brief] Bathroom: slim 25 cm oak cabinet and 28 cm towel tower could not retain the checked 60 cm access around fixed fittings; floor storage omitted, mirror provided and additional storage in shower room.
[catalog] Living: washable-sofa search returned sand Dalton fabric sofa without explicit removable/washable cover specification; washability remains unverified.
[catalog] Living: selected oak dining table has rectangular corners; rounded/softened dining edges not verified.
[catalog] Bedroom 1: textile washability is not specified by the catalog.
[catalog] Office: 2.18 m window needs a neutral glare-control shade; blind search returned 0.94–1.54 m, curtains 2.10 m too short or 2.80 m too wide for 2.27 m wall. Custom shade remains needed.
[catalog] Office: selected ergonomic chair has black mesh; pale ergonomic equivalent not selected.
[catalog] Children: dinosaur artwork search returned no suitable dinosaur art; rug washability unverified.
[brief] Children: no dedicated clothing wardrobe in bedroom; six additional hall bins store folded children's clothing. Dedicated cushioned reading chair, low table and lamp added in reviewer revision.

Reviewer: The rug is too small and almost entirely hidden beneath the bed. (Bedroom 1)

requests: Please furnish our new flat in Orion on the top floor. We are Arman (36) and Siranush (34) Petrosyan with two kids, Tigran (7) and Nare (4). Arman is a game developer at a studio in Yerevan and works from home four days a week: he needs a real office with a 160 cm desk, two monitors, a good chair, shelves for his board-game collection and a door he can close for calls. The small reading room next to the bedrooms is his office. Siranush is a pediatric dentist, out early, back at six; in the evenings she reads and does pilates at home, so she wants a clear spot for a yoga mat in the living room. Tigran and Nare share one bedroom for now: Tigran loves dinosaurs and Lego and needs a little desk for homework, Nare still naps and loves drawing. They need two beds (a bunk bed is fine if it is safe), lots of low toy storage they can reach themselves, a soft rug to play on and a reading nook. We take the other bedroom: a queen bed, a wardrobe and a dresser, nothing fancy. The big living room with the kitchen is where everything happens: a dining table for six (grandparents come every Friday), a large sofa that survives kids, a TV for movie nights, and a corner where the kids can play without toys taking over the whole room. The balcony: two chairs and a small table for morning coffee, plus plants. Style: bright Scandinavian with warm oak, soft pastels, rounded corners (no sharp glass tables with kids), washable fabrics. We dislike dark colours and anything fragile. Budget: 7,500,000 AMD for furniture.
